title: Autosuggest remediation drafts & incident runbook snippets from recent traces
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: On-call responders spend time writing initial incident summaries and first-pass remediation steps. We lack a lightweight, operator-safe assistant that pre-populates a runbook fragment and suggested remediation commands derived from the most relevant traces, logs and top error traces for the incident. Goal: build an "autosuggest remediation drafts" feature that attaches to new PagerDuty incidents (and a Slack incident channel) and provides: 1) a one-paragraph incident summary synthesizing top spans and error signatures, 2) 2-3 prioritized suggested remediation steps (human-editable), 3) reproducible short commands or queries (kubectl, curl, SQL, or diagnostic scripts) and links to the minimal set of traces/log ranges used to generate the suggestions. The output should be clearly labeled as auto-generated, editable in the Console, and included in the PagerDuty/Slack payloads as a suggested runbook snippet. The pipeline must sample traces responsibly, respect PII/data retention policies, and provide an operator override to suppress auto-generation per-service.
acceptance_criteria:
1) When a high-severity PagerDuty incident is created for a service with tracing enabled, the system posts a 'Suggested remediation' block to the incident's Slack channel and attaches a draft runbook snippet to the PagerDuty incident within 60s of incident creation.
2) The draft contains: a short summary (<=3 sentences), 2-3 prioritized remediation bullets, and at least one reproducible diagnostic command or query.
3) All suggestions include transparent provenance: time window, trace IDs (up to 5), and a link to the Console trace viewer.
4) Operators can edit the draft in the Console and save to the service runbook. Edits are recorded in the incident timeline.
5) The system exposes toggles per-service to opt-out of autosuggestions.
6) Sampling rules ensure no more than 1% of traces across incidents are retained for autosuggest artifacts; all retained artifacts follow retention and redaction policies.
7) Security review sign-off obtained and logging shows no sensitive fields in generated outputs.
technical_notes: Architecture: lightweight enrichment service (autosuggest-agent) subscribes to incident events from the incident-broker. On PD incident creation: 1) agent queries recent span-index service -> fetch top error groups for the service in the last 5 minutes, 2) pull full traces for top N groups (N=3 by default) from trace-store via read API, 3) run a deterministic summarizer (small deterministic heuristic pipeline + optional LLM classifier with explicit prompt templates) to produce summary + remediation suggestions + diagnostic commands. Attachments: produce a JSON artifact stored in artifacts-store (S3, encrypted) with pointer added to PD incident and slack block. Privacy: before storage/generation run redaction on spans/attributes and apply KMS envelope. Rate limits: backoff if trace-store throttle > 50ms latency; fall back to 'insufficient data' message. Observability: instrument latency, errors, and sampling rate metrics (autosuggest.latency_ms, autosuggest.errors, autosuggest.samples_kept).
